title: Primary 4 Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
seo_title: P4 Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Mixed numbers, improper fractions and their relationship
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice: improper fractions and mixed numbers with models and number lines, converting, comparing and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The denominator tells you how many parts make 1 whole, and it stays the same when you change between improper fractions and mixed numbers.
body_html:
Proper fractions, improper fractions and mixed numbers

A proper fraction is less than 1: the numerator is smaller than the denominator. An improper fraction is 1 or more: the numerator is equal to or greater than the denominator. A mixed number is a whole number and a proper fraction together.

Proper fractionImproper fractionMixed number
34741 34
2555 (= 1)2 25

Improper fractions from a model

The denominator tells you how many equal parts make 1 whole. Count all the shaded parts for the numerator.

The same picture shows 1 full bar and 34 of another bar, so 74 = 1 34.

Improper fraction to mixed number: divide

Divide the numerator by the denominator. The answer is the whole number. The remainder is the new numerator. The denominator stays the same.

Example

Write 114 as a mixed number.

11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3. That is 2 wholes and 3 quarters.

Answer: 2 34

Mixed number to improper fraction: multiply and add

Change the wholes into parts, then add the parts of the fraction.

Example

Write 2 13 as an improper fraction.

2 × 3 = 6 thirds. 6 + 1 = 7 thirds.

Answer: 73

Compare and order

Write the numbers in the same form first, for example all as mixed numbers. Compare the whole numbers, then the fractions.

Example

Which is greater: 114 or 2 14?

114 = 2 34. Both have 2 wholes, and 34 is more than 14.

Answer: 114

Word problems: draw a model

When the same small amount is repeated, draw a bar of equal units. Count the units to get an improper fraction, then change it to a mixed number.

Example

Each cup holds 14 ℓ of bandung. Priya filled 11 cups. How much bandung did she pour?

11 units = 11 quarters = 114 ℓ. 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3.

Answer: 2 34 ℓ

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
74 = 1 37 (using the numerator as the denominator)The parts are still quarters: 74 = 1 34
2 13 = 63 (forgetting to add the numerator)2 × 3 = 6, then 6 + 1 = 7: 73
Writing 78 for 7 quarters shaded in 2 bars (counting all the parts in both bars)The denominator is the number of parts in 1 whole: 74
Thinking 114 is greater than 3 because 11 is a big numberChange it: 114 = 2 34, which is less than 3

faq.q: What is taught in P4 fractions?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students learn mixed numbers and improper fractions and change one into the other. They also compare fractions, find a fraction of a set, and add and subtract fractions with denominators up to 12.

faq.q: How do I explain improper fractions to my child?
faq.a: Use bars or paper circles. Shade 7 quarters across two bars: that is 7/4, and it is also 1 whole bar and 3/4 of another, so 7/4 = 1 3/4.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with mixed numbers?
faq.a: Changing the denominator, as in 7/4 = 1 3/7. The parts are still quarters, so 7/4 = 1 3/4. Another common slip is 2 1/3 = 6/3; the 1 third must be added, so 2 1/3 = 7/3.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Mixed numbers, improper fractions and their relationship are part of Fractions in the MOE 2021 Primary 4 Standard Mathematics syllabus. Students use these skills again in Primary 5 when they add, subtract and multiply mixed numbers.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. Count the shaded parts: there are 7. So the bars show 7 quarters = 74. The denominator is 4 (the parts in 1 whole), not 8 (the parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. Count the shaded parts: there are 5. So the bars show 5 thirds = 53. The denominator is 3 (the parts in 1 whole), not 6 (the parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. Count the shaded parts: there are 8. So the bars show 8 fifths = 85. The denominator is 5 (the parts in 1 whole), not 10 (the parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 2 equal parts, so each part is 12. Count the shaded parts: there are 5. So the bars show 5 halves = 52. The denominator is 2 (the parts in 1 whole), not 6 (the parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 6 equal parts, so each part is 16. Count the shaded parts: there are 11. So the bars show 11 sixths = 116. The denominator is 6 (the parts in 1 whole), not 12 (the parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 8 equal parts, so each part is 18. Count the shaded parts: there are 13. So the bars show 13 eighths = 138. The denominator is 8 (the parts in 1 whole), not 16 (the parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 4 equal parts. 9 parts are shaded, so it shows 9 quarters = 94. Do not use 12 (all the parts in the 3 circles) as the denominator.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 3 equal parts. 7 parts are shaded, so it shows 7 thirds = 73. Do not use 9 (all the parts in the 3 circles) as the denominator.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 6 equal parts. 13 parts are shaded, so it shows 13 sixths = 136. Do not use 18 (all the parts in the 3 circles) as the denominator.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 5 equal parts. 12 parts are shaded, so it shows 12 fifths = 125. Do not use 15 (all the parts in the 3 circles) as the denominator.

items.q: How many fifths are there in 3 wholes?
items.e: 1 whole = 5 fifths. So 3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths.

items.q: How many sixths are there in 2 wholes?
items.e: 1 whole = 6 sixths. So 2 wholes = 2 × 6 = 12 sixths.

items.q: How many eighths are there in 4 wholes?
items.e: 1 whole = 8 eighths. So 4 wholes = 4 × 8 = 32 eighths.

items.q: You want to shade 114 using bars that are each cut into 4 equal parts. How many bars do you need?
items.e: Each bar holds 4 quarters. 11 quarters fill 2 bars (2 × 4 = 8) and 3 more are left over, so you need 1 more bar. 2 + 1 = 3 bars.

items.q: You want to shade 92 using bars that are each cut into 2 equal parts. How many bars do you need?
items.e: Each bar holds 2 halves. 9 halves fill 4 bars (4 × 2 = 8) and 1 more is left over, so you need 1 more bar. 4 + 1 = 5 bars.

items.q: Which of these is an improper fraction?
items.e: In an improper fraction, the numerator is equal to or greater than the denominator. In 75, 7 is greater than 5, so 75 is improper. 57 and 34 are proper fractions, and 1 27 is a mixed number.

items.q: Which of these is a proper fraction?
items.e: In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator. 8 is smaller than 9, so 89 is proper. 98 and 1010 are improper fractions, and 1 19 is a mixed number.

items.q: Which of these is a mixed number?
items.e: A mixed number has a whole number and a proper fraction together. 3 12 has 3 wholes and 12. 52 is an improper fraction, 13 is a proper fraction and 4 is a whole number.

items.q: Only one of these is an improper fraction. Which one is it?
items.e: The numerator can also be equal to the denominator. 66 = 1 whole, and it is an improper fraction. So the answer is 66. 56 and 67 are proper fractions.

items.q: In the fraction 74, what does the 4 tell you?
c: Each whole is cut into 4 equal parts
items.e: The denominator tells you how many equal parts make 1 whole. In 74, each whole is cut into 4 equal parts (quarters), and the numerator 7 tells you there are 7 quarters.

items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full, so that is 2 wholes. The last bar has 1 of 3 parts shaded: 13. So the shaded part is 2 13.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. The arrow is 2 marks after 1. So it shows 1 23.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.

items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. The arrow is 5 marks after 2. So it shows 2 56.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. The arrow is 1 mark after 1. So it shows 1 14.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 13?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. Go to 2, then 1 more mark. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 35?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. Go to 2, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34. Go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 116?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 116 = 1 56. Go to 1, then 5 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: 2 35 lies between which two whole numbers?
items.e: 2 35 is 2 wholes and a bit more. It is more than 2 but less than 3, so it lies between 2 and 3.

items.q: 175 lies between which two whole numbers?
items.e: 175 = 3 25 (17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2). That is more than 3 but less than 4, so it lies between 3 and 4.

sets.title: Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers

items.q: Write 74 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3. That is 1 whole and 3 quarters left over. The denominator stays 4. So 74 = 1 34.

items.q: Write 113 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 11 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 2. That is 3 wholes and 2 thirds left over. The denominator stays 3. So 113 = 3 23.

items.q: Write 135 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 13 ÷ 5 = 2 remainder 3. That is 2 wholes and 3 fifths left over. The denominator stays 5. So 135 = 2 35.

items.q: Write 176 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 17 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 5. That is 2 wholes and 5 sixths left over. The denominator stays 6. So 176 = 2 56.

items.q: Write 124 as a whole number.
items.e: 124 means 12 quarters. Every 4 quarters make 1 whole: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 124 = 3.

items.q: Write 198 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 19 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 3. That is 2 wholes and 3 eighths left over. The denominator stays 8. So 198 = 2 38.

items.q: Write 2310 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 23 ÷ 10 = 2 remainder 3. That is 2 wholes and 3 tenths left over. The denominator stays 10. So 2310 = 2 310.

items.q: Write 257 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 25 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 4. That is 3 wholes and 4 sevenths left over. The denominator stays 7. So 257 = 3 47.

items.q: Write 319 as a mixed number.
items.e: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 31 ÷ 9 = 3 remainder 4. That is 3 wholes and 4 ninths left over. The denominator stays 9. So 319 = 3 49.

items.q: Write 2 13 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 33, so 2 wholes are 2 × 3 = 6 thirds. Add the 1 third more: 6 + 1 = 7. The denominator stays 3. So 2 13 = 73.

items.q: Write 1 34 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 44, so 1 whole is 1 × 4 = 4 quarters. Add the 3 quarters more: 4 + 3 = 7. The denominator stays 4. So 1 34 = 74.

items.q: Write 3 25 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 55, so 3 wholes are 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add the 2 fifths more: 15 + 2 = 17. The denominator stays 5. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: Write 2 56 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 66, so 2 wholes are 2 × 6 = 12 sixths. Add the 5 sixths more: 12 + 5 = 17. The denominator stays 6. So 2 56 = 176.

items.q: Write 4 12 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 22, so 4 wholes are 4 × 2 = 8 halves. Add the 1 half more: 8 + 1 = 9. The denominator stays 2. So 4 12 = 92.

items.q: Write 1 78 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 88, so 1 whole is 1 × 8 = 8 eighths. Add the 7 eighths more: 8 + 7 = 15. The denominator stays 8. So 1 78 = 158.

items.q: Write 3 310 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 1010, so 3 wholes are 3 × 10 = 30 tenths. Add the 3 tenths more: 30 + 3 = 33. The denominator stays 10. So 3 310 = 3310.

items.q: Write 5 23 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 33, so 5 wholes are 5 × 3 = 15 thirds. Add the 2 thirds more: 15 + 2 = 17. The denominator stays 3. So 5 23 = 173.

items.q: Write 2 49 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 99, so 2 wholes are 2 × 9 = 18 ninths. Add the 4 ninths more: 18 + 4 = 22. The denominator stays 9. So 2 49 = 229.

items.q: Wei Ming wrote 74 = 1 37. What mistake did he make?
c: He found the wrong whole number
He used 7 as the denominator instead of 4
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3, so the whole number 1 and the 3 left over are right. But the parts are still quarters, so the denominator must stay 4: 74 = 1 34.

items.q: Mei Ling wrote 2 13 = 63. What mistake did she make?
c: She forgot to add the 1 third
items.e: 2 wholes = 2 × 3 = 6 thirds, which is right. Then she must add the 1 more third: 6 + 1 = 7. So 2 13 = 73. 63 is only 2 wholes.

sets.title: Compare and order mixed numbers and improper fractions

items.q: Which is greater: 114 or 2 14?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 114 = 2 34, 2 14. So 114 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 2 23 or 73?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 2 23, 73 = 2 13. So 2 23 is greater. A big numerator does not always mean a big number.

items.q: Which is greater: 175 or 3 35?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 175 = 3 25, 3 35. So 3 35 is greater. A big numerator does not always mean a big number.

items.q: Which is greater: 2 58 or 198?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 2 58, 198 = 2 38. So 2 58 is greater. A big numerator does not always mean a big number.

items.q: Which is greater: 1310 or 1 110?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 1310 = 1 310, 1 110. So 1310 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 4 12 or 72?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 4 12, 72 = 3 12. So 4 12 is greater. A big numerator does not always mean a big number.

items.q: Which is greater: 236 or 3 16?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 236 = 3 56, 3 16. So 236 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 1 49 or 169?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers: 1 49, 169 = 1 79. So 169 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 2 12 or 94?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers in quarters: 2 12 = 2 24, 94 = 2 14. So 2 12 is greater. A big numerator does not always mean a big number.

items.q: Which is greater: 116 or 1 23?
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers in sixths: 116 = 1 56, 1 23 = 1 46. So 116 is greater.

items.q:

Which number is the greatest?

items.q:
Which number is the smallest?

c: 83, 2 13, 53
2 13, 83, 53

c: 136, 1 56, 2 56
1 56, 136, 2 56
2 56, 136, 1 56

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
3 12, 134, 154
c: 134, 3 12, 154
3 12, 154, 134
3 12, 134, 154
154, 3 12, 134
items.e: Write them as mixed numbers in quarters: 3 12 = 3 24, 134 = 3 14, 154 = 3 34. So the order is 134, 3 12, 154.

items.q: Which number is between 2 and 3?
items.e: 2 = 84 and 3 = 124. 114 = 2 34, which is between them. 74 = 1 34 and 32 = 1 12 are less than 2; 134 = 3 14 is more than 3.

items.q: Which number is greater than 3?
items.e: 3 wholes = 93. Only 103 (= 3 13) is more than 93. 93 is equal to 3, not greater than 3.

items.q: Each cup holds 14 ℓ of bandung. Priya filled 11 cups. How many litres of bandung did she pour? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Model: 1 unit = 14 ℓ, so 11 units = 11 quarters = 114 ℓ. 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3, so 114 = 2 34 ℓ.

items.q: Mrs Lim bought 7 packets of sugar. Each packet has a mass of 12 kg. What is the total mass of the sugar? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 7 packets of 12 kg = 7 halves = 72 kg. 7 ÷ 2 = 3 remainder 1, so the total is 3 12 kg.

items.q: Mdm Wong cut each kueh lapis into 6 equal slices. She sold 17 slices. How many kueh lapis did she sell? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Each slice is 16 of a kueh lapis, so 17 slices = 176. 17 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 5. She sold 2 56 kueh lapis. The denominator stays 6, not 17.

items.q: Mr Tan cut some watermelons into 4 equal slices each. His class ate 15 slices (shaded). How many watermelons did the class eat? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 15 slices = 154 of a watermelon. 15 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 3, so the class ate 3 34 watermelons.

items.q: One round of the school field is 13 km. Zhi Hao ran 8 rounds on Sports Day. How far did he run? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 8 rounds of 13 km = 8 thirds = 83 km. 8 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 2, so he ran 2 23 km.

items.q: Ryan drinks 13 ℓ of milk every day. How much milk does he drink in 1 week? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 7 × 13 ℓ = 7 thirds = 73 ℓ. 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1, so he drinks 2 13 ℓ.

items.q: Devi reads a storybook for 12 h every day. How many hours does she read in 5 days? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 5 × 12 h = 5 halves = 52 h. 5 ÷ 2 = 2 remainder 1, so she reads 2 12 h (2 h 30 min).

items.q: Siti has a ribbon 3 25 m long. She cuts it into pieces. Each piece is 15 m long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: Change 3 25 m to fifths: 3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths, and 15 + 2 = 17 fifths. So 3 25 = 175. Each piece is 1 fifth, so she gets 17 pieces.

items.q: Mr Rahman bought 3 12 kg of rambutans. He packed them into bags of 12 kg each. How many bags did he fill?
items.e: 3 12 = 72 (3 × 2 = 6 halves, and 6 + 1 = 7 halves). Each bag holds 1 half, so he filled 7 bags.

items.q: Mr Kumar has 2 34 ℓ of paint. He pours it into small tins. Each tin holds 14 ℓ. How many tins can he fill?
items.e: 2 34 = 114 (2 × 4 = 8 quarters, and 8 + 3 = 11 quarters). Each tin holds 1 quarter, so he can fill 11 tins.

items.q: Ali spent 74 h on his Science project. How long is that in hours and minutes?
items.e: 74 = 1 34. 34 h = 3 × 15 min = 45 min (because 14 h = 15 min). So it is 1 h 45 min.

items.q: Jun Jie walked 94 km at Gardens by the Bay. Chloe walked 2 12 km. Who walked further?
items.e: 94 = 2 14. 2 12 = 2 24. 2 24 is more than 2 14, so Chloe walked further.

items.q: Jug A has 134 ℓ of water. Jug B has 3 12 ℓ of water. Which jug has more water?
items.e: 134 = 3 14 (13 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 1). 3 12 = 3 24. 3 24 is more than 3 14, so Jug B has more water. The bigger numerator 13 does not make Jug A bigger.

items.q: Nurul cycled 113 km at East Coast Park. Mei Ling cycled 3 13 km. Who cycled further?
items.e: 113 = 3 23 (11 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 2). 3 23 is more than 3 13, so Nurul cycled further.

items.q: Hui Min has three ribbons. The red ribbon is 2 14 m, the blue ribbon is 74 m and the green ribbon is 52 m long. Which ribbon is the longest?
c: They are all the same length
items.e: Use quarters: 2 14 = 94, 74, and 52 = 104. The greatest is 104, so the green ribbon is the longest.

items.q: Raju's ribbon is 2 35 m long. Kavya's ribbon is 125 m long. How much longer is Raju's ribbon?
items.e: Change 2 35 to fifths: 2 × 5 + 3 = 13, so 2 35 = 135. 135 − 125 = 15 m. (13 − 12 = 1, and the parts are still fifths.)

items.q: Farah needs 3 kg of flour to bake pineapple tarts for Chinese New Year. She has 94 kg of flour. How much more flour does she need?
items.e: 3 kg = 124 kg. 124 − 94 = 34 kg. Check: 94 = 2 14, and 2 14 + 34 = 3.

items.q: Mrs Ng had 3 m of wire. She cut off 5 pieces. Each piece was 14 m long. How much wire was left? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Model: 3 m = 12 quarters, so the bar has 12 units of 14 m. She cut off 5 units. 12 − 5 = 7 units are left: 74 m = 1 34 m.

items.q: A hawker had 4 14 kg of rice. She cooked 94 kg of it for chicken rice in the morning. How much rice was left?
items.e: Change 94 to a mixed number: 94 = 2 14. Then 4 14 − 2 14: the fractions are the same, so only the wholes are left: 4 − 2 = 2. So 2 kg of rice was left.

items.q: At a class party, there were 3 kaya cakes. Each cake was cut into 8 equal slices. The children ate 19 slices (shaded). How much cake was left?
items.e: 3 cakes = 3 × 8 = 24 slices. 24 − 19 = 5 slices left. Each slice is 18 of a cake, so 58 of a cake was left. (The children ate 198 = 2 38 cakes.)
